frequency_question: How often do threatened secondary sanctions against major foreign banks for energy procurement materialize into formal punitive actions within a comparable window?
membership_rule: Includes instances where the primary sanctioning authority publicly warned or formally investigated systemically important foreign commercial banks for energy transactions with heavily sanctioned states, where resolution occurred within a multi-year enforcement window. Excludes generic diplomatic demarches without explicit financial cutoff threats.
window: Within a 36-month tracking window from initial major escalation.

cases.name: Iran Sanctions Act enforcement against European banks (2010-2012)
CAATSA secondary sanction warnings on non-US financial institutions regarding Russian energy (2017-2019)
Section 1045 of the National Defense Authorization Act implementations involving Chinese banks and North Korean/Iranian channels (2013-2015)
Hong Kong Autonomy Act secondary banking sanctions designations (2020-2022)

coverage_note: 4 named; believed to represent the total population of major systemic secondary banking sanction confrontations of this specific class.
known_gaps: Excludes minor or non-public administrative settlements that did not involve formal designation or waiver grants.
skeleton: Enumerate major sanction regime escalation cycles involving potential systemic foreign bank cutoffs since 2000.
multiplier: 4 distinct historical escalation epochs with comparable structural friction.
validity_reason: The geopolitical and structural mechanics governing sovereign currency dominance and major bank compliance thresholds evolve slowly over decades.
